review_comments:
What is the problem, and why does this fix it?

The framework is already making sure that created namespaces are unique. Why is that not enough?

Please see `Special notes for your reviewer:` section of the pr's description. As the audit log showing, two test suites in ephemameral.go is running in parallel and leads to name collisions on the clusterrolebinding resources. 

```
One (namespace is ephemeral-9424-1906) creates the clusterrolebinding resource psp-csi-hostpath-role-ephemeral-9424. (success)
Other (namespace is ephemeral-9424-26)  creates the clusterrolebinding resource psp-csi-hostpath-role-ephemeral-9424. (fail)
One (namespace is ephemeral-9424-1906)  deletes the clusterrolebinding resource psp-csi-hostpath-role-ephemeral-9424. (success)
```

the root cause is that they're sharing the baseName.
Why is the namespace not unique?
Or rather, why is psp-csi-hostpath-role-ephemeral-9424 not unique?
Please wait a moment, my modification does not seem to be correct, I need to investigate further

> Why is the namespace not unique?

namespace  is unique but the psp-csi-hostpath-role-ephemeral-9424 not unique.

I need to investigate further.

Hi @pohly, I thinks the UniqueName of the e2e framework is broken by the csi-driver cleanup function. when ginkgo execs cleanup function, this func is called before it cleanup resources created by the PrepareTest func of csi-driver. 

When two testsuites are running in parallel and they're using the same name of TestSuiteInfo, if the first testsuite is finished and the cleanup function is being called, prehaps the driver namespace is deleted and cluster-scoped resources is still existing, the second testsuite will be failed  because of resource confiliction if it is started with the same namespace.

A possible solution is to call the DriverCleanupFunc function after cleaning up resources.

cc @pohly

`DeferCleanup` runs first-in-last-out. So if the driver gets installed first, it also should get de-installed after all resources that get created later.

A log file that shows creation and deletion would go a long way towards clarifying whether everything happens in the right order.

Another possibility: could it be that `Delete` returns for a resource, but the resource still exists? I'm fairly certain that `kubectl delete` does extra work to block until completion of the delete. `Delete` alone is not enough, that just asks for deletion.

> could it be that Delete returns for a resource, but the resource still exists? 

It's impossible for the `clusterrolebinding` resource in this case.

Hi @pohly I'm wondering the reason why we need delete test and csi-driver namespaces in the [generateDriverCleanupFunc](https://github.com/carlory/kubernetes/blob/25a37d13329ba32cc9a674786da765b44ff93f6f/test/e2e/storage/drivers/csi.go#L1007). those namespaces can be deleted by AfterEach action hooks.

**testsuite 1: Testpattern: Generic Ephemeral-volume (block volmode) (late-binding)**

the test namespace is ephemeral-9424 and the driver namespace is ephemeral-9424-26.

**testsuite 2: Testpattern: CSI Ephemeral-volume (default fs)**

the test namespace is ephemeral-9424 and the driver namespace is ephemeral-9424-1906.

**the root cause I think**

Above info from the audit log of the pr description. We can find name collisions of the test namespace. According to the creation namespace logic of the e2e test framework, it is impossible unless the ephemeral-9424 namespace has already been deleted by a testsuite when the framework of the other testsuite create a namespace.

I agree with the analysis. But that brings me back to my earlier question: why is the namespace being allowed to get deleted while entities like a service account that was used by a test in that namespace still exist?

We need to:
- verify that this happens (via logging)
- prevent it from happening (by waiting for actual removal of the object, if that is the reason)
